extracted.intended_audience: researchers, publishers, librarians, and readers interested in research integrity and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: A year-in-review blog post summarizing counts, trends, and notable developments in retractions for 2022, and describing related projects, tools, and partnerships of Retraction Watch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual retraction rate (retractions per papers published)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions of a given year’s publications expressed as a percentage/share of papers published in science and engineering (the post notes the annual rate is now about 8 in 10,000 papers published).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this metric to track trends over time; be aware that spikes (e.g., 2015) can reflect backlog/lag in retractions rather than contemporaneous increases. Increased scrutiny by sleuths and discovery of paper mills can drive growth in this rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute number of retractions per year
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw count of papers retracted in a given year (example figures in the post: 119 retractions in 2002; 4,600+ retractions in 2022; Retraction Watch Database total >37,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for year-to-year comparisons and public communication; interpret alongside publication volume and rate metrics to understand scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-retraction / lag effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The elapsed time between publication and eventual retraction, which can cause retrospective spikes in annual retraction counts (the post cites 2015 as a reflection of such lag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for long tails when analyzing yearly retraction counts — some retractions occur many years after publication and will influence trend interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness/coverage of a retraction database
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which a database captures known retractions (the post states Retraction Watch Database has about three times as many retractions as PubMed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Database completeness matters for downstream uses (research, alerts, policy). The site invites users to report retractions not in the database to improve coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperability/usefulness of retraction data for external tools and indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how the retraction dataset is integrated into reference managers and indexing services (the post notes the database powers retraction alerts in EndNote, Papers, and Zotero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical integration increases the dataset's impact by preventing unknowing citation of retracted work and by enabling alerting workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy criterion: exclusion based on formal findings of scientific misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarivate used the Retraction Watch Database to exclude researchers 'found to have committed scientific misconduct in formal proceedings conducted by a researcher’s institution, [or] a government agency' from their list of Highly Cited Researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This illustrates a concrete policy/application: formal institutional or government findings of misconduct can be used as a basis for exclusion from honorific lists or metrics-based recognitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of hijacked journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of journals that have been hijacked/fraudulently presented (the post announces the launch of the Retraction Watch Hijacked Journal Checker in partnership with Anna Abalkina).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools that detect hijacked journals support database quality and protect researchers; the announcement implies detection is a recognized dimension of maintaining scholarly integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing unknowing citation of retracted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts and guidance aimed at stopping researchers from unknowingly citing retracted literature (the post references an invited editorial titled 'How to Stop the Unknowing Citation of Retracted Papers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing this problem involves database completeness, alerting systems, and editorial/publisher practices; the post highlights it as a substantive problem requiring action.
